clue.text: Include in the deal the drier yield

parts.note: to throw something in is to add it to a bargain at no extra charge
taken as written
a towel is what dries you after a bath

explanation.surface: A card player or trader agrees to add a tea towel to the bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from boxing, where a corner tosses a towel into the ring to concede, so it means surrender.

clue.text: Over year, plant is economically efficient

indicators.note: in a down clue the plant word sits over, above, the year letter

parts.note: thrift is a pink-flowered coastal plant, also called sea pink

explanation.surface: A plant is praised as an efficient performer, year after year.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careful with money uses resources sparingly, which is economical efficiency.

clue.text: Lush climbing plant in bigger container

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker, as is a toper

explanation.surface: A lush climbing plant has outgrown its pot and needs a larger one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for the plant, but it is the noun for a drunkard; 'climbing' turns TOPER into REPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a houseplant into a new, usually larger, pot is the gardener's verb for this.

clue.text: Emblem of warring faction, otherwise unfamiliar

indicators.note: something unfamiliar is not in its usual form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heraldic badge of some fighting side is said to be strange or alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' rearranges OTHERWISE. The Wars of the Roses were fifteenth-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of York used this flower as its badge in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Close down early — but not entirely

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the words down early, run together across the gap

explanation.surface: Something almost closes down ahead of schedule, though not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Near as an adjective means at a short distance, nearby.

clue.text: How garden tool has cut into border

indicators.note: the tool word goes into the middle of the word how, splitting it

parts.note: taken as written
an edger is a tool for trimming lawn edges

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a gardening implement came to slice into a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of bushes often marks the boundary of a field or garden.

clue.text: Triple crown — primarily, that is annual rugby award

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A rugby trophy for winning the Triple Crown is given each year.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the Triple Crown is won by a home nation beating the other three; here it is the Pope's three-tiered crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal headdress is a three-tiered crown, a jewelled ornamental headpiece.

clue.text: Prepared for fight, said to attack vigorously

indicators.note: said to marks that the words heard are spelt differently from the entry

parts.note: to wade in is to set about something or someone with energy

explanation.surface: A boxer got ready for a bout and was reported to fight hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Wade and weighed are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are put on the scales before a bout to confirm their weight class.

clue.text: Bloodsucker hit upon a victim

indicators.note: in a down clue the hit word sits on top of the victim word

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
prey is a hunted victim

explanation.surface: A bloodsucking creature strikes at the unfortunate creature it targets.
explanation.definitionFit: This eel-like fish fastens onto other fish with its sucker mouth and feeds on their blood.

clue.text: Carpet salesman needs money from abroad -about one million

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative

indicators.note: the foreign currency goes around the letters for one and million

parts.note: the rand is the South African currency
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A carpet seller wants foreign currency worth about a million.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like the rug a salesman sells, but it is the verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone, from being called onto the boss's rug, is to rebuke them.

clue.text: Man given a vote up front, in principle

indicators.note: the article and the vote are placed before the island abbreviation

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot with a cross, X
IOM stands for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man is handed a vote in advance, at least in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth taken as a starting point for reasoning is a basic principle.

clue.text: Mechanic with more qualifications

definitions.meaning: comparative of fit, meaning more suitable or better qualified

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an engineering tradesman, and the comparative of fit as suitable.

clue.text: Encountered a figure of speech — such as this.

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: of speech means the number word is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: four is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: Someone says they came across a figure of speech, offering the remark itself as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure four, as spoken, can be written PHOR; 'such as this' points at the clue's figurative phrase as an example of the device.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue calls a number a figure of speech, an image used figuratively, the very device being named.

clue.text: Fret about a backward plant

indicators.note: backward means the whole assembly is read from right to left
the word for fret goes around the letter a

parts.note: to fret is to worry

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously frets over a plant that is slow to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside WORRY to make WORRAY, which 'backward' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Achillea, a feathery-leaved herb with flat flower heads, is a common wild plant.

clue.text: Tape and string employed in harness? Good!

indicators.note: the string word is used inside the harness word

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's harness
cord is thin string

explanation.surface: Someone praises using tape and string to rig up a harness.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape can mean a stored audio or video recording.

clue.text: Jumpy, sad. and moody when judgment has to be faced

definitions.text: when judgment has to be faced

indicators.note: something jumpy moves about restlessly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nervous, gloomy person awaits the moment of reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Judgment in Christian belief is the day the world ends and souls are judged.

clue.text: Savage old racehorse upset our group

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the horse's name is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: Red Rum was a famous horse that won the Grand National three times in the 1970s
us means our group

explanation.surface: A fierce former racehorse unsettled our team.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'upset' horse is read upwards in this down clue. The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase, run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage as an adjective means violently brutal, inclined to kill.

clue.text: We will argue over name used too often

parts.note: we'll is the contraction of we will

indicators.note: over means the word for argue is turned round

parts.note: to row is to argue

explanation.surface: A couple will fight about which name is overused.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase that is hackneyed is threadbare from overuse.

clue.text: Bird dog used by the Spanish

parts.note: a cocker spaniel is a breed of dog
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A bird dog is trained by Spanish hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' reads as a gundog, but splits into the definition and the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male domestic fowl is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Stand on table contains a representative cake

indicators.note: the table stand holds the representative within it

parts.note: a cruet is a stand holding salt, pepper and condiment bottles
MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A dish on a table holds a cake for a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a soft griddle cake, toasted and buttered, common at British teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: This spongy round griddle bread is loosely classed as a teacake.

clue.text: European field marshal

definitions.meaning: a native of France is a European
Sir John ... was a British field marshal who commanded in the First World War

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a person from France, and the surname of a famous British commander.

clue.text: Pacific burial ceremony tool?

parts.note: Pacific means peacemaking, not the ocean: the tool is the one buried in the idiom for making peace

explanation.definitionFit: To bury this small axe is the idiom for ending a quarrel.

clue.text: Frees excited slave after remarkable run

indicators.note: the rearranged slave comes after the rearranged run
remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged
excited means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An agitated slave is freed after an extraordinary escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' turns RUN into UNR; 'excited' turns SLAVE into AVELS.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a knot or tangle is to free it, undoing it.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as just '24' with no 24-across in the grid; no cross-reference gives VISIT and the real clue is missing.

clue.text: Tyrant to achieve what Lady Macbeth couldn't?.

definitions.text: to achieve what Lady Macbeth couldn't?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., to remove a spot, which Lady Macbeth failed to do with her bloodstained hand

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare, Lady Macbeth sleepwalks crying 'Out, damned spot!'
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who wields power cruelly is a tyrant.

clue.text: Cut irregularities off tree

definitions.meaning: to ... wood is to shave it smooth
the ... tree, common in London streets

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: smoothing wood with a blade, and a broad-leaved shade tree.

clue.text: Knock out dwarf before reaching final

indicators.note: stopping before the final letter means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to stunt is to dwarf growth

explanation.surface: A small player knocks someone out just before the final of a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze someone senseless with a blow.

clue.text: Minister has no time for questions, curiously

indicators.note: the minister word loses the letter for time

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A busy cleric has strangely little time for anyone's queries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pries asks nosy questions, inquiring out of curiosity.

clue.text: One fixes bones with hot potatoes in stew

indicators.note: potatoes in a stew are chopped up and mixed, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bone-setter dishes up hot potatoes in a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats the skeleton and muscles by manipulating bones and joints.

clue.text: After dieting, one can economise

definitions.meaning: after slimming you can pull your waistband in a notch
to economise is to spend less

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cutting back spending, as if eating less to make a belt fit tighter.
